alex: Quick summary — ran a cohort-aware replay on the 2026-02-10 prod traces with the new anonymization+weighting pipeline. Two actionable items surfaced:
- ~0.4% of traces show non-deterministic outputs vs prod (diffs in logits after KV warmup)
- 95th tail latency regressed by ~18% on 80-token flows due to a kernel fallback path

maya: can you paste the exact replay command and the anonymization steps? also attach the small diffs if possible :eyes:

alex: sure, command I used:
```bash
./replay_harness \
  --trace traces/2026-02-10.bin \
  --anon-map maps/anon_map_v3.json \
  --seed 42 \
  --sample-stratified "route:weight=by_tokens" \
  --preserve-client-order \
  --cohort=signup_region \
  --emit-pprof=pprof_out.pb
```
Anonymization notes: hash-prefix IDs (sha256 -> first 12 chars) + route bucketing by hashed endpoint, then per-route weight adjustment so high-volume routes don't drown small ones. We also drop user metadata fields except region and language.

liam: thanks. two quick thoughts — (1) determinism misses often come from KV cache warmup differences when we replay requests slightly reordered or when we don't emulate the exact prefix‑cache hits. Try forcing cache entries warm by replaying the first N requests of each cohort as a warmup phase. (2) kernel fallback: which kernel selector config did you use? fallback to 'safe' kernels can blow up tail.

alex: I used the runtime default selector (auto). Here are the high-level perf numbers (subset):
```
baseline hosted run (prod): median 11ms, p95 42ms, tokens/s 3500
replay run (current): median 12ms, p95 49.6ms, tokens/s 3300
```
And nondet diffs: 0.4% of 12k sampled sessions had token-level logits mismatch > 1e-4 after 5 tokens.

zoe: quick repro checklist:
- confirm replay preserves request ordering and original inter-arrival spacing (we sometimes compress time during synthetic bursts)
- seed RNGs in runtime and replay harness (`--seed`) so op-level nondeterminism is minimized
- KV warmup: run `--warmup-head 100` per cohort to populate KV cache before measuring
- kernel selection: pin a kernel to compare apples-to-apples, e.g. `RL_KERNEL_FORCE=fast_attn_v2`

liam: to add — there's also subtle nondeterminism from CUDA graph reuse + JIT kernel dispatch. For parity runs, run with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` + `RL_DISABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` for a deterministic baseline (slower but useful for diffs).

alex: ran a quick follow-up with cohort warmup and kernel pinning. command diff:
```bash
./replay_harness --trace traces/2026-02-10.bin --anon-map maps/anon_map_v3.json --seed 42 \
  --sample-stratified "route:weight=by_tokens" --preserve-client-order --cohort=signup_region \
  --warmup-head 200 --env RL_KERNEL_FORCE=fast_attn_v2
```
Result snippet:
```
with warmup+pin: median 11.2ms, p95 43ms, tokens/s 3450, nondet 0.02% (from 0.4%)
```
So warmup cut most nondet diffs. Kernel pin reduced the p95 regression significantly.

replay-bot: automated-run-summary: id=run-1987654321, traces=12000, sample=0.1, warmup=200, kernel_pin=fast_attn_v2, nondet_rate=0.0002, p95=43.0ms

maya: nice. next steps I suggest:
- document the anonymization mapping and share small example of the hashed mapping for review (no real IDs)
- bake `--warmup-head` into the default cohort-aware mode of the harness, maybe `--warmup-percent 0.01` to scale with trace size
- run an apples-to-apples kernel comparison across the common models we serve and add to the perf dashboard (route-level breakdown)

zoe: also flag to runtime: let's add a `replay_mode` that sets deterministic flags automatically (`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING`, seed, disable graph reuse) so every parity run is reproducible. I'll file a tiny RFC.

alex: thanks — I'll open a PR with the harness changes (warmup as default for cohort runs) and attach the anonymized diff artifacts. Planning a canary tomorrow with pinned kernel for 2 hours and then roll back if any user-facing anomalies show up. :thumbsup:

liam: ping me when you open the PR, I'll add the CUDA-graph notes and the small pprof snippet that showed the kernel fallback hotpath.

zoe: great work, this is the reproducible path we needed. :100:
